claim: D-166 says every request that arrives on an open keep-alive connection after STOPPING began gets 503 with Connection: close. On TinyHttpd this holds only until the adapter stop of D-162 starts. From then on, HttpServer.stop calls onServerStopping, which closes idle keep-alive connections without an answer (a request racing the close is dropped with lingerClose), and in-flight responses are committed with Connection: close because isStopping() is true. Later requests on those connections get a closed socket, not a 503. A T44 test written to D-166 as stated would fail or flake.

No item says whether the TinyHttpd adapter sets TinyHttpd's maxRequestBodyBytes (default -1). D-219's mapping of TinyHttpd size-overrun body exceptions to 413 only matters if the limit is set. If it is set, a request whose declared Content-Length is above it gets a fixed plain-text 413 from RequestParser before dispatch. That 413 skips onError, the standard error JSON and the access log, which breaks D-129 (onError receives framework 413 errors), and it is missing from the D-400 list of transport-level rejections.

D-401 reads 'wave 6 adds temporary-file cleanup and wave 7 adds WebSocket closing and SSE closing as before-wait participants', which can be parsed as making temp-file cleanup a before-wait participant. If it runs before the adapter stop, it deletes spool files of uploads still in flight, which D-342 lets complete.

D-419 makes the WebSocket message limit configurable. TinyHttpd also enforces a separate per-frame limit, maxFramePayloadBytes (default 1 MiB), which closes with 1009. No item maps the configured limit onto it, so raising the message limit above 1 MiB still closes connections that send one large unfragmented frame.

D-440 rewrites only the kotlin.md examples. docs/api/README.md and express-migration.md also have Kotlin examples that pass the now-nullable req.body(...) result straight to a service call. Under D-349 these compile only if the test stubs take nullable parameters, so the docs teach passing T? onward.

TinyHttpd accepts an asterisk-form 'OPTIONS * HTTP/1.1' and passes the raw path '*' to the handler. No item says how the core treats a raw path that does not start with '/' (reject with 400, or answer server-wide OPTIONS). I-021 requires the same status on every adapter.

CLAUDE.md names only NaruServe-api and NaruServe-servlet as modules and names NaruServe-api as the API 21 check target. D-002 adds seven modules and D-027 extends animal-sniffer to them, but only D-365 (the sample exception) updates CLAUDE.md, so project instructions go stale after wave 1.
object.md 9.3 requires testing symlink/TOCTOU, but no item covers a path component swapped for a symlink between the canonical check and the open.
